# BMI Patterns by Income Group

## Audience Question

Audience: a public-health analyst preparing a short classroom briefing on descriptive BMI patterns in the prepared NHANES Health Equity dataset.

Question: among included adults aged 20-80, how does average BMI vary across NHANES cycles for the selected income group?

## Setup

<!--
Source: assignments/assignment07-dashboard/dashboard-starter.qmd.
All four R chunks are retained unchanged from the course-provided starter.
-->

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)  # AI-EDIT(2026-06-23): tidyverse-default — consolidated core library() calls into library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

candidate_paths <- c(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
)

data_path <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)][1]
if (is.na(data_path)) {
  stop("Could not find examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")
}

nhanes <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Control

The selected income group determines which records appear in the table and chart. This static dashboard uses a source-code control: changing `selected_income` and rendering again updates the output.

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-control
available_income_groups <- sort(unique(na.omit(nhanes$IncomeGroup)))
selected_income <- "Low Income (<1.3)"

if (!selected_income %in% available_income_groups) {
  selected_income <- available_income_groups[1]
}

selected_income
```

Available groups are `"Low Income (<1.3)"`, `"Middle Income"`, and `"High Income (>3.5)"`.

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-summary
dashboard_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    Age >= 20,
    Age <= 80,
    IncomeGroup == selected_income,
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(Cycle)
  ) |>
  group_by(Cycle) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(dashboard_summary)
```

## Visualization

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-plot
ggplot(dashboard_summary, aes(x = Cycle, y = mean_bmi, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = "#2f6f73") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, color = "#2f6f73") +
  labs(
    title = paste("Mean BMI for", selected_income),
    subtitle = "Adults age 20-80 in the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom dataset",
    x = "NHANES cycle",
    y = "Mean BMI",
    caption = "Descriptive, unweighted classroom summary. Missing BMI, income group, cycle, and out-of-cohort ages are excluded."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

## Interpretation

<!--
# AI prompt: Expand the Interpretation for a public-health analyst. Explain chart points and counts, the omitted intervening cycle, equal spacing of cycle labels, automatic Y-axis scaling, different samples, and the absence of uncertainty intervals or statistical tests. Verify the actual duration of the 2021-2023 cycle against CDC documentation. Retain the descriptive, unweighted limits and keep all R code unchanged.
# Verified: Confirmed the August 2021-August 2023 collection dates using CDC documentation; compared all four R chunks with the starter; checked the CSV cycle labels, low- and middle-income outputs, automatic axis scaling, and the visible limitation.
-->

Each point is the average BMI of included adults aged 20-80 in the selected income group for one NHANES cycle; the table shows how many records contributed. These unweighted classroom summaries describe the included records and do not show that income caused BMI to change or that the pattern applies to all US adults.

The prepared dataset moves directly from the 2017-2018 cycle to the 2021-2023 cycle, with no intervening cycle included. Although the 2021-2023 label spans three calendar years, it represents approximately two years of collection, from August 2021 to August 2023 ([CDC documentation](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/continuousnhanes/overviewbrief.aspx?Cycle=2021-2023)). Cycle labels are equally spaced rather than positioned by elapsed time; the connecting line does not show intervening annual measurements or an annual rate of change. Each cycle summarizes a different sample of adults, rather than changes in the same individuals. The vertical scale adjusts to the selected group, so compare table values rather than apparent heights or slopes across group settings. No uncertainty intervals or statistical tests are shown.

## Limitation

This starter is unweighted and descriptive. It does not account for NHANES survey design, does not estimate national prevalence, and should not be used to make causal claims about income and BMI.
